notes: Local `main` is stale (v0.9.53); the real PR delta vs origin/main is the single commit c15a190. Review covered that commit only.
Verified: go build/vet clean, full `go test ./...` passes (proxy 31s, store 13s), `tsc --noEmit` passes for the web changes.

Tests genuinely exercise the new code path: fake IdP (discovery + JWKS with RSA/EC keys) via httptest, tokens signed RS256/PS256/ES256, negative cases (expired, nbf, wrong issuer, typ=ID, HS256, cnf, unknown kid, missing sub, suspended/unregistered account, viewer role without mcp:use) each assert 401 + specific error.code + audit event count; off-by-default test asserts no WWW-Authenticate and 404 metadata; REST paths assert no challenge and token refused.

internal/proxy/mcp_oauth.go:395 — email fallback trusts the token's `email` claim without checking `email_verified`. This mirrors the existing web sign-in merge-by-email (keycloak_handlers.go:279), so it is not a new class of risk, but a realm with self-registration and unverified emails could let a new Keycloak user open an existing account's /mcp access. Consider requiring email_verified=true for the fallback in a follow-up.

internal/proxy/mcp_oauth.go:371 — azp match against mcp.oauth.audience means any token minted for the listed client passes regardless of aud (by design, documented in ADMIN_GUIDE). Acceptable given the admin opts in per client id.

internal/proxy/keycloak.go:jwksMissInterval — the 30s unknown-kid refetch throttle is process-wide and shared with the web login JWKS lookup; a stream of forged kids on /mcp can delay a legitimate key rotation pickup by up to 30s for web sign-in too. Minor, documented.

internal/proxy/mcp_oauth.go:276-288 — ES* alg is not pinned to its curve (ES256 with a P-384 key would still verify). Harmless since the key comes from the realm JWKS, but deviates from RFC 7518 strictness.

internal/proxy/mcp_oauth.go:139/478 — when neither mcp.oauth.resource nor a Keycloak redirect URI is set, the resource identifier and metadata come from requestOrigin(), which honours X-Forwarded-Host, and the metadata is served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`. A shared cache could retain a spoofed resource value for 5 minutes. Documented as a last resort; production guidance says to set the resource.
No token introspection/revocation: Keycloak logout does not invalidate already-issued access tokens until exp (documented; recommends short token lifetime).
Scope in commit: docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.pdf and docs/USER_GUIDE.pdf regenerated as part of the feature docs; no unrelated refactors or dependency changes found.
Feature is default-off (mcp.oauth.enabled=false, permission group `security`), no migrations, fully revertable.
